## TL;DR

The task drawer's Details tab no longer opens with the full metadata form. The Depends on picker, Type, Priority, Area and Story (or Assigned to, when stories are off) now sit behind a single summary button, one or two lines tall, such as `feature · p2 · web · no story · no dependencies` or `bug · p1 · web · depends on #0002, #0003`. Clicking it opens a shared-dialog modal with the same controls. Edits still go into the drawer's existing draft, so the existing Save bar saves them with the same API call as before. The prerequisite picker now shows selected dependencies as chips above the search box, with `None` when nothing is set. The headless WebKit layout test and the jsdom interaction tests cover the collapsed summary at 375, 768 and 1280 px, the modal's geometry, and each field's edit and save.

## Work and rationale

The change lives in three places. `TaskDrawer.vue` replaces the inline block with a `task-meta-summary` button. A `metaSummary` computed builds the summary text from `draft`, not from the saved task, so the one-line summary tracks what the modal is editing. A root-level `Dialog` (`task-meta-modal`) holds the existing controls, reusing the `et-dependencies`, `et-area` and `et-story` ids so that existing selectors and the shared `AreaPicker` keep working. I kept the modal inside the drawer's draft rather than giving it its own save path. That matches "changes save the same way they do today" and keeps the API calls unchanged.

The modal closes when the drawer's active task changes, via a watch on `ui.active?.id`. Without that, opening a different task while the modal was up could show another task's draft.

`TaskDependencyPicker.vue` moves the selected list to the top as chips. Each chip keeps the existing `Remove dependency <id>` aria-label, so the picker tests that drive removal by label still pass. The picker is shared with the New task panel, so that panel's inline picker also gets chips and `None`. I did not collapse the New task panel, because the task names only the drawer.

The dependency rows that used to sit above the picker (`dep-row`) are gone. They showed each prerequisite's blocker state (`not merged`, `cancelled`, `archived`, `done`) and let you click through to it. The collapsed summary lists ids, and the modal shows titles through the chips, but the blocker state and the click-through are lost from the Details tab. This is the one behaviour change I'd ask a human to confirm. I removed the now-unused `dependencyRows`, `openDependency` and `DependencyChip` import, and the `.dep-list`/`.dep-item*` styles. `.dep-chip-icon` stays, because `DependencyChip.vue` still uses it.

Styling is in `style.css`, next to the other modal shells: `.task-meta-summary` clamps to two lines with `-webkit-line-clamp`, and `.task-meta-modal.drawer-wrap.drawer` mirrors the `sm-modal` centred shell. Under 480 px the modal's two-column rows stack, and the modal's action button meets the 44 px touch floor.

## Approaches tried

I considered keeping the dependency rows inline above the summary, which would have kept the blocker state visible. That breaks the two-line acceptance criterion, so I dropped it. I also considered a separate `TaskMetaModal.vue` component. I kept the modal inside `TaskDrawer.vue` because it reads and writes the drawer's `draft`, `draftAreaList`, `storySelectValue` and related computeds. Splitting it out would mean threading all of those through props and emits, with no gain for a single-use dialog.

For tests, I first tried opening the modal in the browser-test harness and measuring `.drawer-wrap`. That hit a strict-mode error, because the modal also carries `drawer-wrap drawer`. The fix was to measure the collapsed drawer and the modal in separate renders, with a dedicated `checkActualModal` for the modal.

## Challenges and blockers

Two test failures were my own mistakes, not product bugs. First, `makeTask` defaults to `type: "bug"`, so my first Type pick was a no-op. I changed the test to pick `chore`. Second, the dependencies UI test mounts without `attachTo`, so the teleported modal never reaches `document.body`. The helper `openTaskDetailsModal` now falls back to the wrapper's own element.

The scoped `repoos check --changed main` gate failed twice on type errors in my test code. The first was a `TS2347` untyped call on `wrapper.element.querySelector`, which I fixed with an `Element` cast. The second was a `setProps` typing mismatch, which I avoided by mounting a second wrapper with the selected value. `vue-tsc` reports many errors in `TaskDrawer.vue` on lines I did not touch. Those predate this change, and the gate's build step does not run `vue-tsc` before the root `tsc` fails, so I did not try to clear them.

## Key learnings

Measuring a collapsed block and its expanded form in one layout pass does not work well. Separate renders, each with its own assertions, are clearer, and the harness already had the shape for that.

A summary that reads from the draft rather than the saved task keeps a collapsed control honest about what Save will send. It also means the test can assert on the summary text right after editing, which is a useful check that the modal's controls are bound to the same draft.

When a test asserts a value is changed, check the fixture's default first. `makeTask` already has `type: "bug"`, so selecting that value looks like a failed edit when it is really a no-op.
